mainTopic: Purifying and washing items from a חטאת in the עזרה: earthenware and copper pots, the כהן גדול's מעיל, and the seven cleaning substances
overview: The גמרא first finishes an earlier discussion: a small torn piece of a garment is impure only מדרבנן, so by תורה law it may be brought into the עזרה to be washed. It then explains two lines of the משנה. A punctured earthenware pot must still be broken because a tiny hole leaves it a vessel. A copper pot with a large hole must still be scoured because it is hammered back into a vessel. Next, ריש לקיש teaches that the כהן גדול's מעיל may not be torn, so it is brought into the עזרה a little at a time, in pieces smaller than three by three, and washed. רב אדא בר אהבה objects that thick garments are not measured by three by three. The גמרא answers that pieces of the מעיל count as important because of the special garment they come from. Finally, the גמרא asks how any garment with חטאת blood can be washed in the מקדש at all, since washing needs seven substances, including urine, and urine may not be brought into the מקדש.

steps.title: The small piece is impure only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question: when רב הונא called the small piece impure, he meant only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impure only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer begun just before this. It says the small torn piece of cloth is impure only by rabbinic decree, not by תורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, it looked as if רב הונא said a piece smaller than the minimum size is still impure, which would stop it from being brought into the עזרה. The answer limits that: by תורה law the piece is pure, and the impurity is only a rabbinic safeguard. So bringing it into the עזרה to wash it is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: It is from the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this line, on the previous daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling: the impurity is only rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The small piece is impure by Torah law and so cannot be brought into the עזרה
steps.terutzMaskana: It is pure by Torah law and impure only מדרבנן

steps.title: Why break an earthenware pot that is already punctured?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about an impure earthenware pot and asks why it must be broken once it already has a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an earthenware vessel that went out and became impure is punctured, brought in, and broken. But the תורה says 'vessel,' and once it is punctured it is not a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and challenges it. A punctured pot is not a vessel anymore, so why does the משנה require breaking it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the earthenware vessel a חטאת was cooked in must be broken. The משנה has the pot punctured first, which makes it pure so it can enter the עזרה. But a punctured pot seems to no longer count as a 'vessel,' so the פסוק's command to break it should not apply anymore.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware (clay) vessel
'The Merciful One,' meaning the תורה
A vessel, something that can hold things

phrases.english: An earthenware vessel that went out, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: it is punctured, brought into the עזרה, and broken there.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'vessel,'
and it is not a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement to break the punctured earthenware pot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires breaking a 'vessel,' but a punctured pot is no longer a vessel

steps.title: A tiny hole leaves it a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The pot was punctured with only a tiny hole, which makes it pure but leaves it a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was punctured with a hole the size of a small root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hole was tiny. That is enough to make the pot pure, but it still counts as a vessel, so it must be broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small hole takes away the pot's impurity, but the pot can still hold things like fruit. So it is still a 'vessel' in the פסוק's sense, and the command to break it still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Was punctured
A small root, a measure for a tiny hole

phrases.english: Where it was punctured with a small root.
phrases.notes: He means a hole only as wide as a small root.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly: the hole is a very small one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any hole stops the pot from being a vessel
steps.terutzMaskana: A tiny hole makes it pure but leaves it a vessel, so it must still be broken
steps.whatToRemember: A hole can be big enough to remove impurity but still small enough that the item counts as a vessel.

steps.title: Why scour a copper pot that has a hole in it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the copper pot and asks why it must be scoured if the hole makes it no longer a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a copper vessel that became impure is broken with a hole, brought in, and scoured and rinsed. But it is not a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a copper pot and asks the same kind of question. Once it has a large hole, it is not a vessel, so why scour it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With copper, a tiny hole is not enough. The pot gets a large hole, which really ends its status as a vessel. Then the תורה's command to scour and rinse the vessel seems not to apply anymore.

keyTerms.meaning: A copper vessel
He breaks it open by making a large hole

phrases.english: A copper vessel, etc. He breaks it open, etc.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording. The משנה goes on: he brings it in, scours it and rinses it.

phrases.english: But it is not a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 2, now about the copper pot.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement to scour and rinse the broken copper pot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scouring applies to a vessel, but a copper pot with a large hole is no longer a vessel

steps.title: He hammers it back into a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The copper pot is hammered and remade into a vessel, so it must then be scoured and rinsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He hammers it and makes it whole again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that after making the hole, he hammers the copper back into a working vessel. Now it is a vessel again and must be scoured and rinsed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large hole made the pot pure and allowed it into the עזרה. Then, once it is fixed back into a vessel, the command to scour and rinse applies again. That is why the משנה requires it.

keyTerms.meaning: Hammers it together, remaking it
Scouring and rinsing, how a copper vessel is cleaned

phrases.english: Where he hammers it back together.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case: the pot is remade into a vessel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pot stays broken, so it is not a vessel and needs no scouring
steps.terutzMaskana: He hammers it back into a vessel, so it must be scoured and rinsed
steps.whatToRemember: Earthenware gets a tiny hole and stays a vessel. Copper gets a large hole and is then remade into a vessel. Either way, the תורה's command still applies.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's robe is brought in bit by bit, not torn
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that an impure מעיל is not torn. It is brought into the עזרה in sections smaller than three by three and washed, because the תורה says it may not be torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: if the מעיל became impure, one brings it in a section smaller than three by three at a time and washes it, because the פסוק says 'it shall not be torn.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new rule. The robe of the כהן גדול cannot be torn to make it pure like other garments, so it is brought in little by little and washed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an impure garment with חטאת blood on it is torn so it can enter the עזרה and be washed there. The מעיל may not be torn, so instead only a piece smaller than the size that can carry impurity crosses into the עזרה at a time, and each piece is washed as it comes in.

keyTerms.meaning: The robe of the כהן גדול
Three by three fingerbreadths, the smallest cloth that can become impure
He washes it
'It shall not be torn'

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A robe that became impure –
phrases.notes: He is talking about the מעיל that got חטאת blood on it and then became impure outside.

phrases.aramaic: מַכְנִיסוֹ בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ וּמְכַבְּסוֹ,
phrases.english: he brings it in less than three by three at a time and washes it,
because it is said: 'It shall not be torn.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of impure garments discussed earlier, adding a special case for the מעיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure מעיל is not torn. It is brought into the עזרה in sections smaller than three by three and washed, because of the command 'it shall not be torn.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the usual method of purifying a garment by tearing it gives way when the תורה forbids tearing, and another method is used instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The מעיל is still a garment that needs washing. Only the method changes: instead of tearing it, it is brought in a little at a time.

steps.title: Thick garments are not measured by three by three
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges ריש לקיש using a משנה that says thick and soft garments are not subject to the three-by-three measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objects: a משנה teaches that thick garments and soft garments are not subject to the rule of three by three!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges ריש לקיש's rule from Step 6 by quoting a משנה about thick and soft garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the מעיל must be brought in pieces smaller than three by three, so that no piece counts as a garment that can be impure. But the משנה says thick garments are not measured by three by three at all, since such a small piece of them is useless. The מעיל is thick, so why worry about pieces of three by three?

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
The thick garments
The soft garments
Three by three fingerbreadths, the smallest piece of cloth that can become impure

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava raises an objection:
The thick garments and the soft ones
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כלים 28:8. The מעיל is a thick garment, so it fits here.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ!
phrases.english: are not subject to the rule of three by three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's method of bringing the מעיל in pieces smaller than three by three.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that the מעיל is brought into the עזרה in sections smaller than three by three.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If thick garments are not measured by three by three, the size limit seems pointless for the thick מעיל.

steps.title: The pieces are important because of the whole garment
steps.stepSummary: Pieces of the מעיל count as important because of the special garment they come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of their source garment, they are considered important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אדא בר אהבה: pieces of the מעיל are different from pieces of other thick garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small piece of thick cloth is not worth anything, so it is not counted. But the מעיל of the כהן גדול is so important that even its small pieces matter. So they can become impure at three by three, and ריש לקיש's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of, because of
Literally "their father", meaning the whole garment they came from
They are considered important

steps.whatToRemember: The thick-garment rule is not cancelled; the מעיל is an exception because of its importance, so its pieces still count at three by three.

phrases.english: On account of their "father" they are considered important.
phrases.notes: "Father" here means the whole מעיל that the pieces came from.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the special importance of the source garment makes the מעיל an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מעיל is thick, so its small pieces should not count, and the three-by-three limit seems unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pieces of the מעיל are important because of the whole garment, so the three-by-three limit still applies.

steps.title: Washing needs urine, which cannot enter the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a garment stained with חטאת blood can be washed in the מקדש, since washing needs seven substances, including urine, and urine may not be brought into the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't washing need seven cleaning substances? For רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: blood of a חטאת and marks of נגעים need seven cleaning substances. And a ברייתא teaches: except that urine is not brought into the מקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how the washing of a garment stained with חטאת blood is done inside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, teaches that removing חטאת blood requires all seven cleaning substances, and one of them is urine. A ברייתא says urine is not brought into the מקדש. So how can the washing, which must be done in the עזרה, ever be done properly?

keyTerms.meaning: Seven cleaning substances used to scrub out a stain
Blood of a חטאת offering that splashed on a garment
Shades of צרעת marks on a garment
Urine

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mention washing at all. The difficulty only works once you know that urine is one of the seven substances.

phrases.english: But doesn't it require seven cleaning substances?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Blood of a sin offering and shades of leprous marks
require the seven cleaning substances;
And it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסִין מֵי רַגְלַיִם לַמִּקְדָּשׁ!
phrases.english: except that urine is not brought into the Temple!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of the pieces to how the washing itself is done in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that a garment stained with חטאת blood be washed inside the עזרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Washing needs all seven substances, including urine. Urine may not enter the מקדש, so the washing could never be done properly there.
